# Analysis of subcellular spatial proteomics data in R {.unnumbered}

## Overview

These materials focus on subcellular spatial proteomics, 

::: {.callout-tip}
### Learning Objectives

You will learn about:

- How mass spectrometry can be used to ...
- The bioinformatics steps involved in processing and analysing subcellular proteomics data.
- How to assess the quality of your data, deal with missing values, and summarise feature-level data to protein-level.
- How to perform ...
:::

### Target Audience

Proteomics practitioners or data analysts/bioinformaticians that would like to learn how to use R to analyse proteomics data.

### Prerequisites

- Basic understanding of mass spectometry.
  - Watch [this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wx4F6kGy1Fs) for an excellent overview.
- A working knowledge of R and the tidyverse.
- Familiarity with other Bioconductor data classes, such as those used for RNA-seq analysis, is useful but not required.

## Citation

<!-- We can do this at the end -->

Please cite these materials if:

- You adapted or used any of them in your own teaching.
- These materials were useful for your research work.

For example, you can cite us in the methods section of your paper: "We carried out our analyses based on the recommendations in Hutchings and Breckels (2026)".

You can cite these materials as:

> Breckels LM, Hutchings C, (2026) "CambridgeCentreForProteomics/course_subcellular_proteomics: Analysis of subcellular spatial proteomics data in R", https://cambridgecentreforproteomics.github.io/course_subcellular_proteomics

Or in BibTeX format:

```
@Misc{,
  author = {Lisa M Breckels and Charlotte Hutchings},
  title = {CambridgeCentreForProteomics/course_subcellular_proteomics: Analysis of subcellular spatial proteomics data in R},
  month = {November},
  year = {2026},
  url = {https://cambridgecentreforproteomics.github.io/course_subcellular_proteomics}
}
```

### Other key references

Data analysis workflow

> Hutchings C, Krueger T, Crook OM, Gatto L, Lilley KS, and Breckels LM
> An updated Bioconductor workflow for correlation profiling subcellular proteomics [version 2; peer review: 3 approved].
> F1000Research 2025, 14, 714 [http://dx.doi.org/10.12688/f1000research.165543.1](http://dx.doi.org/10.12688/f1000research.165543.1)

The `QFeatures` R/Bioconductor package.

> Gatto L, Vanderaa C: QFeatures: Quantitative features for mass spectrometry data.
> R package version 1.23.1.
> 2023.
> Reference Source

The `pRoloc` R/Bioconductor package.

> Gatto L, Breckels LM, Wieczorek S, Burger T, Lilley KS. Mass-spectrometry-based spatial
>  proteomics data analysis using pRoloc and pRolocdata. Bioinformatics. 2014 May 1;30(9):1322-4.
>  doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btu013. Epub 2014 Jan 11. PubMed PMID: 24413670; PubMed Central
>  PMCID: PMC3998135.

Case-study data

> McCaskie K, Hutchings C, Feret R, et al. Localization of Organelle Proteins Using Data-Independent Acquisition (DIA-LOP). Mol Cell Proteomics. 2025;24(9):101047. [doi:10.1016/j.mcpro.2025.101047](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40783120/)
